children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for just one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex!

To help determine your eligibility, could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship and living situation with Alex.

Are you responsible for Alex, meaning does he live with you and do you pay for things like his food, clothes, and other necessities?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't actually live with me, but I do contribute towards his upkeep - I help out with money for his needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to ask a few more questions.

Does Alex live with someone else, such as his other parent or another family member, who might also be responsible for him or claiming Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with his mum. I'm not sure if she's claiming Child Benefit for him or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

Could you tell me, does Alex's mum have the main day-to-day responsibility for looking after him? In other words, is she the one who primarily takes care of his daily needs like meals, getting him to school, and so on?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, she does - she's the one looking after him day-to-day since he lives with her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining the situation.

Based on what you've told me, Alex's mum has the primary day-to-day responsibility for looking after him since he lives with her and she takes care of his daily needs.

Under the Child Benefit rules, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, and the person who is primarily responsible for the child (i.e., the one who the child lives with and who looks after them on a day-to-day basis) has priority for the claim.

While it's good that you contribute financially towards Alex, because he lives with his mum and she has the main responsibility for his care, she would be the person eligible to claim Child Benefit for him rather than you.

Let me now provide you with my formal assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex:**
- Although Alex is 9 years old and within the qualifying age for Child Benefit, the key requirement is that the claimant must be primarily responsible for the child.
- Alex lives with his mum, and she has the main day-to-day responsibility for looking after him.
- Under Child Benefit rules, only one person can claim for a child, and priority is given to the person with whom the child lives and who is mainly responsible for their care.
- While your financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep are commendable, they do not give you priority over his mother for claiming Child Benefit.

**What this means:**
Alex's mum would be the person eligible to claim Child Benefit for him. If she isn't already claiming, she may wish to apply.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

reasonings: Alex is 9 years old and would normally qualify for Child Benefit based on his age. However, the key eligibility requirement is that the claimant must be 'responsible' for the child. A person is considered responsible for a child if the child lives with them, OR they contribute to the cost of looking after the child at least at the same rate as Child Benefit. In this case, Alex lives with his mother, who has the main day-to-day responsibility for him. When a child lives with one parent who has primary responsibility, that parent has priority to claim Child Benefit. Since Alex does not live with the claimant and his mother is his primary carer, the claimant is not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child, and priority goes to the person with whom the child lives.
